ModMetaData.name: Perfectly Generic Item Patched (unofficial)
ModMetaData.author: Ogliss - 1.6 adapted by Nelim
ModMetaData.description:
UNOFFICIAL. This mod is published without the original author's explicit consent. If the original author contacts me to request its removal, I undertake to take it down promptly.
Update of Ogliss' Perfectly Generic Item to the latest RimWorld version.
I am not the author of this mod. The idea, the design and the original code are entirely Ogliss', made for MercuryDoll - all I did was the work needed to make it run on the latest version. Credit goes to them; mistakes in the update are mine. If the original author comes back to it, or asks me to take this down, I will.
Original mod: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2169353373
What it does
When you remove a mod from an ongoing save, every item it added is lost, and the log fills with "could not load reference to ThingDef". This mod catches those missing things as the save is read and turns each one into a perfectly generic item - a stack of green placeholder blocks - the way Starbound does. Nothing disappears silently, and you can haul, sell or destroy the leftovers at your own pace. A mod setting makes them despawn on their own a few seconds after loading.
The generic item is also a stuff, so it can stand in for a wall or a garment whose material is gone. It is excluded from every material picker, so it is never offered for construction, never used by generated bases, and never handed out as a quest reward.
What changed in the update
The mod was dead on the latest version, not merely flagged red. Its Harmony setup patches all its hooks in one call, one of those hooks was gone, and the exception took the whole class down with it - including the missing-def replacement that is the entire point of the mod.
- BaseGenUtility.IsCheapWallStuff no longer exists in the latest version. The patch that used it kept the generic item out of generated settlement walls; that job is now done by allowedInStuffGeneration on the def itself, which is what the game checks in its place. The patch is gone. - StuffProperties.soundImpactStuff was renamed soundImpactBullet, which was throwing an XML error on every load. - The three remaining hooks - StuffProperties.CanMake, SketchGenUtility.IsStuffAllowed, ThingSetMakerUtility.IsDerpAndDisallowed - and BackCompatibility.BackCompatibleDefName still exist with the same signatures, and were recompiled unchanged against the current reference assemblies.
Three defects were fixed along the way, which is why this is "Patched" rather than a plain update.
- Translation injections go through BackCompatibleDefName as well. The mod answered them too, so a missing def's translated labels were written onto the generic item, renaming it in-game. Def injections are now left alone. - When RimWorld's own compatibility chain successfully renamed an old def, the mod overrode that answer with the generic item anyway, losing a thing that could have been recovered. It now only steps in when nothing else resolved. - The optional StuffedFloors compatibility patch was registered as a prefix while being written as a postfix, so it read a result that did not exist yet. It is now registered as a postfix.
A French translation was added, and the item is now hidden from StuffedFloors' floor list as originally intended.
Safe to add to an ongoing save - that is what it is for. Removing it mid-save turns any generic items still lying around into the same missing-reference errors it was there to absorb, so destroy them first.
AI-GENERATED
The update work and this description were written with Claude Code (Anthropic), and the mod icon generated with an image model, under human direction and review. Stated openly: designing with these tools is my job. The mod's own design and code remain Ogliss'.
LICENCE
Ogliss' mod declares no licence, so this update carries none either - relicensing someone else's code is not mine to do. It follows the established Workshop practice for reviving abandoned mods: explicit credit, a link to the source mod, and immediate removal on the author's request.
THANKS
Ogliss, for the mod, and MercuryDoll, for whom it was written.
Ludeon Studios, for the back-compatibility chain this mod hooks into.
Andreas Pardeike, for Harmony.
Claude Code (Anthropic).
Full attribution, including what was taken and what was fixed: https://github.com/vbardales/Rimworld-Perfectly-Generic-Item-Patched/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md
